{"assignees":[],"labels":[],"last":[{"a":"Ben-Home","assoc":"NONE","at":"2026-11-04T23:07:47Z","body":"The decisive detail is that those requests carried no `Authorization` header at all. A token that had expired or been revoked would still be sent and rejected, so an absent header says the client failed to attach a credential it presumably still holds. Your log agrees: no `/mcp/token` between the 401 and the following sign-in, so no refresh was attempted. Nothing was refused, because nothing was presented.

That makes one existing log field worth checking before anything else: what those six 401 responses carried in `WWW-Authenticate`.

RFC 6750 section 3.1 says, of a request with no credentials, that "the resource server SHOULD NOT include an error code or other error information", and its own example of that case is a bare `Bearer realm="example"` challenge. The `invalid_token` code is defined for a token that was presented and failed, and the client "MAY request a new access token and"},{"a":"jellejacob","assoc":"NONE","at":"2026-11-05T08:48:31Z","body":"Thanks, that was the right field to check. Measured against the live endpoint today (2026-11-05):

```
POST /mcp/mail, no Authorization header
HTTP/2 401
www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://ai.drdocks.nl/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/mail"

POST /mcp/mail, Authorization: Bearer <malformed token>
HTTP/2 401
www-authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="https://ai.drdocks.nl/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/mail", error="invalid_token"
```

-- `tokenExchangeCallback` on every exchange (code + refresh); the nightly
-- `grant-idle-prune` job reconciles this table against KV and revokes the
-- rows that went quiet (oauth/grant-sweep.ts).
--
-- No FK to `users`: KV is authoritative for grants and this table is a stamp
-- ledger the sweep reconciles against it (seeding missing rows, deleting
-- orphans), so a NOT NULL child of `users` would only add a parent-rebuild
-- landmine (conventions §G1) for integrity the sweep already provides.
CREATE TABLE oauth_grant_activity (
  grant_id        TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  user_id         TEXT NOT NULL,
  client_id       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
  created_at      INTEGER NOT NULL,
  last_refresh_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

-- The sweep's read: oldest-quiet first.
CREATE INDEX idx_grant_activity_idle ON oauth_grant_activity(last_refresh_at);
-- Per-user cleanup (suspend/delete revokes every grant a user holds).
CREATE INDEX idx_grant_activity_user ON oauth_grant_activity(user_id);

/**
 * Single source of truth for the OAuthProvider config.
 *
 * `index.ts` constructs the live provider; admin tooling (e.g. the
 * OAuth-clients viewer) constructs a read-only `OAuthHelpers` instance
 * via `getOAuthApi(opts, env)` and MUST use the identical KV+path
 * config so the helpers point at the same data the live provider
 * wrote. Extracted here so we can't drift.
 *
 * The `defaultHandler` is plumbed through as a parameter because
 * helpers paths (listClients, lookupClient, etc.) never invoke it —
 * admin code can pass a stub, while `index.ts` passes the real Hono
 * app.
 */

import type { ExportedHandler } from '@cloudflare/workers-types'
import type {
  OAuthProviderOptions,
  TokenExchangeCallbackOptions
} from '@cloudflare/workers-oauth-provider'
import { McpSessionDO } from '../mcp/session-do'
import type { Env } from '../env'
import { mcpResourceUrl } from '../util/mcp-host'
import { stampTokenExchange } from './login-activity'

const NOOP_HANDLER: ExportedHandler<Env> = {
  fetch: () => new Response('not used by admin helpers', { status: 500 })
}

/**
 * Access-token lifetime: 7 days, not the library's 1 h default.
 *
 * Claude's hosted connector (Desktop / claude.ai) does not refresh when an
 * expired access token gets a 401 on /mcp — it shows the user a "Reconnect"
 * prompt, and that click is what runs the (succeeding) refresh_token grant.
 * With 1 h tokens every idle gap longer than an hour cost a prompt (2026-11
 * field finding: 401 bursts on /mcp, each followed only by a refresh after
 * the user acted, never a server-side rejection). A longer token makes the
 * prompt roughly weekly at worst.
 *
 * Why this is safe here: access tokens live in KV, so suspend/delete
 * (`revokeAllUserGrants`) still kills them instantly, and the session DO
 * re-checks user status on init. The cost is a longer useful life for a
 * leaked bearer. Must stay well below `MCP_LOGIN_IDLE_DAYS` so an active
 * client always refreshes inside the idle window.
 */
export const MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 7 * 24 * 60 * 60

/**
 * A login lasts as long as it keeps refreshing (see oauth/login-activity.ts).
 *
 * Both TTLs below are passed as `undefined` on purpose — the library then
 * writes the grant and the DCR client record to KV with NO expiration, and
 * expiry becomes ours to decide. That is the only way to get a sliding
 * session out of this library: `refreshTokenTTL` is stamped once, at the
 * authorization-code exchange, and the refresh path re-saves the same
 * absolute instant (it even refuses a `refreshTokenTTL` returned from the
 * token-exchange callback). `clientRegistrationTTL` behaves the same way
 * from the registration moment, so leaving it at its 90 d default would cap
 * the login independently — the final refresh would just fail
 * `invalid_client` instead of `invalid_grant`.
 *
 * What replaces them: `tokenExchangeCallback` stamps every exchange into
 * `oauth_grant_activity`, and the nightly `grant-idle-prune` job revokes
 * grants that have been silent for `MCP_LOGIN_IDLE_DAYS`. Instant lockout is
 * unaffected — suspend/delete still calls `revokeAllUserGrants`, and the
 * session DO re-checks user status on init.
 *
 * `env` is required: the canonical resource (below) is derived from it, and
 * admin tooling building `OAuthHelpers` from these same options (see the
 * module header) must name the identical resource. Those helpers never
 * exchange a token, so the callback being installed there is inert.
 *
 * Resource (workers-oauth-provider 1.x): every grant and access token is
 * bound to exactly one resource, compared exactly — see `mcpResourceUrl`.
 * Only `/mcp` is served. The legacy HTTP+SSE endpoint (`/sse`) was dropped
 * at the 1.x upgrade: 1.x cannot cover two sibling paths with one resource,
 * the SSE transport is deprecated in MCP, and no stored grant was bound to
 * it (2026-11 KV scan of the largest deployment: 0 of 444).
 */
export function oauthProviderOptions(
  env: Env,
  defaultHandler: ExportedHandler<Env> = NOOP_HANDLER
): OAuthProviderOptions<Env> {
  // apiHandlers requires ExportedHandlerWithFetch (Required fetch);
  // our handler carries `fetch` at the value level but its declared
  // type doesn't line up exactly, so the map is cast once.
  const apiHandlers = {
    '/mcp': McpSessionDO.serve('/mcp', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' })
  } as OAuthProviderOptions<Env>['apiHandlers']
  return {
    apiHandlers,
    defaultHandler,
    resourceMetadata: { resource: mcpResourceUrl(env) },
    authorizeEndpoint: '/oauth/authorize',
    tokenEndpoint: '/oauth/token',
    clientRegistrationEndpoint: '/oauth/register',
    // Explicit `undefined` — it overrides the library defaults (30 d / 90 d)
    // through the options spread, and is what makes the KV records
    // expiration-less. See the note above before "simplifying" these away.
    refreshTokenTTL: undefined,
    clientRegistrationTTL: undefined,
    accessTokenTTL: MCP_ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS,
    tokenExchangeCallback: (opts: TokenExchangeCallbackOptions) => stampTokenExchange(env, opts),
    scopesSupported: ['mcp']
  }
}

#!/bin/bash
# Read-only: one user's MCP login chain on yukitools since 2026-11-07.
# Prints grant/client id prefixes + timestamps only (no tokens, no emails).
set -euo pipefail
set -a; . /Users/stevenn/Projects/satisa/ctxlayer-ops/.tenant-secrets/yukitools-cf.env; set +a
API="https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/accounts/$CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID"
AUTH="Authorization: Bearer $CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN"
DB=$(curl -s --max-time 30 -H "$AUTH" "$API/d1/database" |
  python3 -c 'import sys,json; r=json.load(sys.stdin)["result"]; print(next(d["uuid"] for d in r if "ctxlayer" in d["name"]))')
SQL="select substr(grant_id,1,6) g, substr(client_id,1,6) c,
 datetime(created_at/1000,'unixepoch') created,
 datetime(last_refresh_at/1000,'unixepoch') last_refresh
 from oauth_grant_activity where user_id like 'ba4b75d6%'
 and created_at > 1762473600000 order by created_at"
python3 -c 'import json,sys; print(json.dumps({"sql":sys.argv[1]}))' "$SQL" |
  curl -s --max-time 60 -H "$AUTH" -H 'content-type: application/json' -d @- "$API/d1/database/$DB/query" |
  python3 -c '
import sys,json
r=json.load(sys.stdin)
if not r.get("success"): sys.exit(str(r.get("errors")))
rows=r["result"][0]["results"]
print("grant  client created (UTC)        last refresh (UTC)")
for x in rows: print(x["g"],x["c"],x["created"],x["last_refresh"])
print(len(rows),"logins since Nov 7")'

# Concurrent refresh_token grants with the same refresh token make connectors disconnect on servers with refresh-token rotation

### MCP server URL

Internal company server.

### Where does the issue occur?

During a conversation (after initial auth)

### Transport used

streamable-http

### Client registration type

Client ID Metadata Document (`https://claude.ai/oauth/mcp-oauth-client-metadata`). Dynamic Client Registration is also offered, but not used by Claude.

### SSE only: Does your server return the expected status code for POST requests?

Not applicable (my server does not use SSE)

### When did you last reproduce this?

2026-10-08 07:18 UTC (production logs). It happens several times a week for several users.

### Browser and OS

Not browser-specific: scheduled tasks and conversations on claude.ai.

### Describe the issue

Several users have to reconnect our custom connector again and again. Scheduled tasks fail because the tools are not available.

Our authorization server rotates refresh tokens (OAuth 2.1, better-auth `oauth-provider`). A refresh token is valid once, and reusing a superseded refresh token outside a 30-second grace window revokes the whole token family. This is the reuse detection recommended for public clients.

The logs show that Claude sends **two `refresh_token` grants with the same refresh token at the same time**. When a conversation or scheduled task starts, Claude opens several `/mcp` requests in parallel. If the access token has expired, each one gets 401, and each one starts its own refresh:

```
2026-10-08 06:04:29.279 UTC  POST /mcp                      401
2026-10-08 06:04:29.295 UTC  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token    400  invalid_grant
2026-10-08 06:04:29.313 UTC  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token    200
2026-10-08 06:04:31.265 UTC  POST /mcp                      401
2026-10-08 06:04:31.948 UTC  POST /mcp                      401
```

The same pattern (two token requests within 20 ms, one 400 and one 200) appears on 2026-10-02 10:52:53 UTC as well. On 2026-10-08 06:04, the `/mcp` requests after the refresh still get 401, so the token from the successful refresh does not seem to be used.

Later, Claude refreshes again with a token that has already been rotated. The server treats it as a stolen token and revokes the family. From then on, every refresh fails and the connector needs a manual reconnect:

```
2026-10-08 06:19:34 UTC  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token    200
2026-10-08 07:18:09 UTC  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token    400  invalid_grant
2026-10-08 07:18:10 UTC  POST /mcp                      401
2026-10-08 07:18:10 UTC  POST /mcp                      401
```

Afterwards our refresh token table was empty for this client. Every token family had been revoked by reuse detection.

**Expected:**

- Claude refreshes a connector's credentials once ("single flight"). Parallel requests that get 401 wait for that one refresh and use its result.
- If one of two refreshes fails with `invalid_grant` while the other succeeds, Claude keeps the tokens of the successful one. It never uses a refresh token again after it has received a new one.

We work around it on our side by retrying a failed refresh grant so that both parallel requests get the same tokens. Other servers with refresh-token rotation will run into the same problem.

### Error details

No error ID was shown. In the UI, the connector asks to connect again. Scheduled tasks report that the tools are not available.


----- Ben-Home [NONE] 2026-10-29T12:04:34Z
The timestamps in your log pin down which race this is, and it changes where the fix has to go.

Look at the ordering in the first burst:

```
06:04:29.279  POST /mcp                     401
06:04:29.295  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token   400  invalid_grant
06:04:29.313  POST /api/auth/oauth2/token   200
```

The failing grant returned **18 ms before** the successful one. So the loser did not present a token that had already been rotated; it presented the same current token as the winner while the winner was still mid-rotation. A post-rotation grace window keyed on "this token was consumed at time T, accept replays until T+30s" does not cover this pair at all, because at the moment the loser is validated no rotation has been committed yet. That is why the 30-second window is not saving you here.

The mechanism that does cover it is single-flight on the token row: serialize concurrent grants for the same refresh token family, let the first one rotate, and answer the rest with the newly issued token instead of `invalid_grant`. In effect, treat a duplicate in-flight grant as idempotent rather than as reuse. Reuse detection is still correct for tokens presented *after* the rotation settles, which is the threat model it is meant for.

The second half of your log says the same thing from the client side:

```
06:04:31.265  POST /mcp  401
06:04:31.948  POST /mcp  401
```

Those are 2 and 2.7 seconds after a 200, so a fresh access token existed and the requests still went out with the old one. Each in-flight `/mcp` request appears to hold its own credential snapshot and refresh independently. That is a client-side single-flight problem: one refresh per credential, with the other requests awaiting its result, and the resolved token propagated to all of them. Worth reporting to Anthropic as its own defect, because server-side deduplication will stop the family revocation but will not fix these trailing 401s.

For your own server in the meantime, the cheapest mitigation that survives both defects: on `invalid_grant` for a token that was consumed within the last few seconds, return the currently valid token for that family if you still hold it, rather than revoking. That converts a hard disconnect into a retry, and leaves the family revoke for genuinely stale tokens. It is a deliberate weakening of strict reuse detection, so it is worth logging loudly whenever it fires so you can tell whether it is still needed once the client side is fixed.

Your "several times a week for several users" rate is consistent with a race that only shows up when a scheduled task or conversation start coincides with an expired access token, which is the case you identified. Nothing here looks like a server misconfiguration.

Update from the server side:

- The concurrent-refresh race is handled now: a refresh that fails with `invalid_grant` is retried after 100/300/900 ms and then gets the stored rotation answer of the winner. Concurrent refreshes no longer revoke the token family.
- It still happened afterwards, though. Claude sent an already rotated refresh token again 10+ minutes after the rotation (no concurrent request involved). With better-auth's 30-second reuse window, that revoked all tokens of the user, and Claude did not attempt another refresh until the user reconnected. It hit two users in the same night. Each failure followed a cold start of a replica by about 10 seconds, so either the rotation response never reached Claude, or a request kept a stale credential snapshot, as you describe.

# Cowork (Claude Desktop): remote connector tools lost mid-conversation with a healthy OAuth session; reconnect registers a new DCR client and open conversations stay without tools

## Summary

A remote MCP connector (Streamable HTTP, OAuth 2.1 with DCR), used from **Cowork in Claude Desktop**, keeps losing its tools in the middle of a conversation. Our server never rejects the user: no 401, no 404, no unknown session, and the OAuth family stays alive. After the user reconnects the connector from Settings → Connectors, the conversation that was already open still has no tools ("the tool does not exist"), and Claude registers a **new DCR client** on every reconnect.

Related: #702 (tools silently lost). In our case the token is valid and the server never returns 401.

## Environment

- Server: `https://hq.flip.legal/mcp` (Streamable HTTP; JSON responses; SSE only for `tools/call` that may elicit; `GET` returns 405, so there is no standalone server stream). Sessions are persisted in Postgres and survive restarts and replicas. Protected Resource Metadata and RFC 8414 metadata are served. Refresh tokens rotate with a 60 s reuse grace window.
- Client: Claude Desktop (macOS) with Cowork. `clientInfo` seen on initialize: `claude-code 2.1.304` (Cowork), `Anthropic/ClaudeAI 1.0.0`, `Anthropic/Toolbox 1.0.0`.
- The server exposes 89 tools. We know the `tools/list` payload is large and we are reducing it.

## Timeline (UTC, 2026-10-20, one user)

- 19:29:54 → 19:49:34: MCP session A is active and its tool calls succeed.
- 19:49:08: Claude sends a new `initialize` (session B) while A is still active. The same OAuth family is used and there is no re-auth.
- 19:51:24: the last request on session B. After that, the user's conversation reports the connector's tools as missing. Our logs show no failed or rejected request from this user in that window; the only error is an unrelated input validation error at 19:42:53.
- 20:19:42: the user reconnects from Settings → Connectors and clicks Allow. **A new DCR client and a new OAuth family are registered.** This user now has 8 DCR clients since 2026-10-15, one per reconnect.
- 20:19:43 to 20:23:03: new sessions open on the new family from `Anthropic/Toolbox`, `Anthropic/ClaudeAI` and `claude-code 2.1.304`.
- After 20:23:03: no requests reach the server. In the conversation that was open before the reconnect, Claude answers that the connector's tools "do not exist".
- In the same hour, `tools/list` was called **80 times** for this user.

Separately, Cowork's local logs on the user's Mac show the device bridge (`wss://bridge.claudeusercontent.com`) closing with code 1006 several times. Tools are also lost when the Mac has not slept.

## Expected

1. A conversation keeps its connector tools when the connection is healthy, or re-initializes on its own without losing them.
2. Reconnecting a connector also restores its tools in conversations that are already open.
3. Reconnecting reuses the registered client instead of registering a new DCR client every time.

## Questions

- Is there a supported way, such as a `notifications/tools/list_changed` channel or a different session policy, for a server to help the client recover its tools in an open conversation?
- Our server now supports CIMD (`client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`, auth method `none`). The docs only publish the CIMD URL for Claude Code. **Can you publish the CIMD URLs used by claude.ai, Claude Desktop, mobile and Cowork?** We need them so a reconnect is recognized as the same client.
- Is 80 `tools/list` calls per hour for a single user expected behavior?

We can share request IDs and exact timestamps privately if that helps.


----- Ben-Home [NONE] 2026-10-27T14:02:37Z
The timeline points at three separate failures, not one, and separating them makes the recovery path server-side only:

1. Two live sessions for one subject. `initialize` at 19:49:08 opened session B while A was still active on the same OAuth family. From then on a request can land on either session, and the conversation stays bound to the one it started with. Nothing in that transition is an error, which is why your logs show no rejected request: the loss is a client-side binding to an inventory the server legitimately still serves.

2. DCR is not reused, and that is why reconnect does not restore tools into open conversations. Eight client_ids since Oct 15 means each Allow click minted a new registration. The open conversation's bindings referenced the previous authorization, so a new client_id and family cannot restore them even though the server is healthy. My suggestion, and the most useful change here: on `POST /register`, hash the client metadata you actually key on (redirect_uris, token_endpoint_auth_method, grant_types, software_id, client_name) and return the existing registration for an identical tuple inside a subject session instead of minting a new one. RFC 7591 section 3.2.1 permits the authorization server to return an existing client for duplicate metadata. That turns reconnect from "new identity" into "refresh the same identity", which is the only version of reconnect that can re-attach an open conversation.

3. 80 `tools/list` calls in an hour with 89 tools is the third. Re-attach is cheap for you and expensive for the client, and large inventories have a second failure mode that looks exactly like this: clients that cap the list (count or payload bytes) drop tools silently and then report "the tool does not exist". Worth measuring whether the missing tools are always the ones late in your ordering.

On your question about `notifications/tools/list_changed`: it cannot cover the case you hit. The notification travels on a live session stream, and you have a 1006 bridge close plus `GET` returning 405, so there is no stream to deliver on when the loss happens. It does help the narrower case where the session survives and the inventory changes, so keep it, but do not expect it to recover an open conversation.

Two things that do work without a client release: keep one active session per (client_id, subject) by returning the same `Mcp-Session-Id` on an `initialize` that arrives with an Authorization header for a family that already has a live session, and add a short grace window before answering 404 for a session id minted recently, answering with a rotated `Mcp-Session-Id` header instead. Keep the spec 404 for genuinely expired sessions.

We build a multi-connector MCP server (corpusiq.io) and hit the same shape: a client re-listing on re-attach while the conversation keeps its earlier snapshot is indistinguishable from a server that dropped the tools. The only levers the server owns are identity stability and list cost.

# Default-endpoint fallback triggered by a transient outage during refresh replaces working metadata and is never undone

### What happened?

Our custom connector uses a pre-registered public client (PKCE, `offline_access`). The authorization server (Keycloak) runs on a different host and is advertised through protected resource metadata. Every night, a maintenance window takes both the authorization server and the MCP server offline for a few hours.

If a background refresh falls into that window, the connector breaks permanently:

1. The refresh against the advertised token endpoint gets a 503.
2. Claude immediately re-runs OAuth discovery against the MCP server. The MCP server is also down, so every discovery request fails.
3. Claude then POSTs the refresh to `https://<mcp-host>/token`, the default endpoint on the MCP server's origin, which is not an OAuth endpoint on our side.
4. From then on, every refresh goes to `https://<mcp-host>/token`, even hours after both services are back. Claude never re-runs discovery and never contacts the advertised token endpoint again.

The refresh token is still valid at the authorization server the whole time. Only a manual disconnect and reconnect recovers the connector. The same connector breaks in claude.ai and Claude Code together.

We understand the default endpoints come from the 2025-03-26 authorization spec ("Fallbacks for Servers without Metadata Discovery"), and the troubleshooting docs describe the same fallback for sign-in. Three things in this case look unintended:

1. The fallback fired on timeouts while the server was down, not on a 404 that would mean the server has no metadata. The server served protected resource metadata and authorization server metadata successfully at connect time.
2. It replaced already discovered, working metadata during a refresh, not during a first sign-in.
3. It is never undone: Claude keeps refreshing against the fallback endpoint after it fails, and does not re-run discovery once the server is reachable again. The 2025-11-25 spec has no default endpoints at all.

### What did you expect to happen?

A 5xx or a timeout during refresh or discovery should be treated as transient: retry later against the token endpoint from the authorization server metadata discovered at connect time. If the fallback is used at all, it should not outlive a failed attempt, and discovery should run again once the server responds.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Serve protected resource metadata whose `authorization_servers` points to an authorization server on another host, with refresh tokens enabled.
2. Add the server as a custom connector and connect.
3. When the next refresh is due, make the authorization server's token endpoint return 503 and make the MCP server unreachable.
4. Restore both.
5. Watch the access logs: refreshes go to `https://<mcp-host>/token`, never to the advertised token endpoint, and the connector stays broken until it is reconnected.

OAuth / Authentication

### MCP Server (if applicable)

Custom server, Streamable HTTP, Keycloak 26.6.4 as authorization server, pre-registered public client

The part that looks like the real defect is the missing re-discovery trigger, not the fallback itself.

Splitting what you observed into three separate conditions helps when arguing for a fix:

1. The fallback fired on a 503 or timeout. Per the 2025-03-26 authorization spec, the default endpoints exist for servers that do not expose metadata discovery at all, which is an absence signal (404 on the well-known paths), not a transport failure. A 503 says come back later, so retrying against a guessed endpoint converts a few hours of planned downtime into a durable misconfiguration.
2. It replaced metadata that had already been discovered successfully. Discovery worked at connect time, so the client had the authorization server token endpoint in hand. A refresh path that re-runs discovery should prefer the cached result and only overwrite it on a 200 that names a different issuer.
3. It is never undone. That is the part that turns an outage into a manual reconnect. A provisional endpoint needs a provenance marker and an expiry, and the next refresh should re-run discovery before using a provisional endpoint a second time.

What you can ship on your side today, without waiting for the client fix: serve the protected resource metadata and the authorization server metadata from something that stays up when the authorization server does not. Both documents are static JSON. Put them behind a long max-age on the MCP host edge, or a CDN in front of it. During the maintenance window discovery then keeps succeeding, the refresh gets its 503 from the advertised token endpoint, and the fallback condition never becomes true. Serving last-known-good metadata from the MCP host origin also makes `https://<mcp-host>/token` a harmless no-op if the fallback does fire, because you can rewrite that one path to the authorization server token endpoint at the proxy.

This failure class is not specific to one client. We run a multi-connector OAuth layer (corpusiq.io) where a connector keeps its own authorization state per account, and the same shape appears whenever a refresh target is cached as a side effect of a failed attempt: the retry logic looks healthy and the connector stays broken until someone disconnects it. The durable fix on both sides is to treat a cached fallback endpoint as a hint that expires, never as configuration.

One more line worth putting in the report: the refresh token stayed valid at the authorization server the whole time, so a refresh scheduler that retries 5xx with jitter across the maintenance window recovers with zero user action. That is a small client change and it removes this class of permanent breakage entirely. 260	The part that looks like the real defect is the missing re-discovery trigger, not the fallback itself.
261	
262	Splitting what you observed into three separate conditions helps when arguing for a fix:
263	
264	1. The fallback fired on a 503 or timeout. A 503 says come back later, so retrying against a guessed endpoint converts a few hours of planned downtime into a durable misconfiguration.
265	2. It replaced metadata that had already been discovered successfully. Discovery worked at connect time, so the client had the authorization server token endpoint in hand. 266	3. It is never undone. That is the part that turns an outage into a manual reconnect. A provisional endpoint needs a provenance marker and an expiry, and the next refresh should re-run discovery before using a provisional endpoint a second time.
267	
268	What you can ship on your side today, without waiting for the client fix: serve the protected resource metadata and the authorization server metadata from something that stays up when the authorization server does not. Both documents are static JSON. Put them behind a long max-age on the MCP host edge, or a CDN in front of it. During the maintenance window discovery then keeps succeeding, the refresh gets its 503 from the advertised token endpoint, and the fallback condition never becomes true. Serving last-known-good metadata from the MCP host origin also makes `https://<mcp-host>/token` a harmless no-op if the fallback does fire, because you can rewrite that one path to the authorization server token endpoint at the proxy.

270	This failure class is not specific to one client. You were right: my first pass only skimmed the last few comments. I have now read every comment on #228, #1194, #1166, #1169, #1224, #1225 and #1274, and two workarounds other operators used fit ctxlayer and are not in place. Neither is confirmed as your cause yet, and nothing is built or deployed.

## Workarounds that apply to us

| Source | What others found | Their workaround | ctxlayer today |
|---|---|---|---|
| #1169 | After one transient failure during refresh or discovery, Claude switches to default endpoints on the MCP host (`/token`, `/register`, `/authorize`) and never re-discovers. | Alias those root paths to the real endpoints; stuck connectors recovered. | Unhandled on `mcp.yukitools.dev`: `POST /token` returns 405, `POST /register` 405, `GET /authorize` serves the SPA. |
| #1194, #1169 | Claude uses its published client identity (CIMD) instead of dynamic registration when the server offers it; one operator reports CIMD sign-in "refreshes normally". | Advertise CIMD support. | Off (`client_id_metadata_document_supported: false`). The library option exists: `clientIdMetadataDocumentEnabled`. |
| #1194 | Claude sends two concurrent refreshes with the same refresh token; the one whose token it keeps can be the invalidated one, and a refused refresh is terminal. | Replay the winner's rotation for 1–24 h instead of returning `invalid_grant`. | Our library only keeps the immediately previous token valid, so the race can bite. Not seen in the logs we read earlier. |
| #1166 | Same shape as ours: Desktop/Cowork, healthy OAuth, a new registration on every reconnect, large tool list. | A commenter suggested returning the existing client for identical registration metadata; nobody reported trying it. | Not done; weakest lead. |

The first row matters most: our earlier log reads were filtered to `/oauth/token` and `/mcp`, so hits on the root paths would never have shown up.

## Workarounds that do not apply

- **Entra scope-on-refresh facade** (most of #228): we are our own authorization server and refreshes return 200.
- **HTTP/2 header casing, client auth on refresh:** already ruled out or not our setup.
- **Own app deleting the connector's session** (the Supabase case): I checked; only admin suspend/delete and the nightly sweeps revoke grants, and the sweeps revoked 0 in the Nov 8 check.

## What I could not do

The classifier blocked my prod read, so I could not check the logs or your login chain since Nov 9. Two things you can run:

- **Workers Logs:** filter `mcp.yukitools.dev`, user agent `python-httpx`, path exactly `/token`, `/register` or `/authorize`, last 7 days. Any hit confirms the #1169 fallback.

```

## Recommendation

Build the root-path aliases and CIMD together. The aliases are harmless even if the log check comes back empty. input.ask: Build CIMD support (with the root-path aliases) for a test release?

content.text:
The chain rules out every refresh-related workaround: since Nov 9 the connector has never refreshed once, yet it re-registered and forced a full sign-in seven times.

## What the rows say

- **Since the 7-day tokens went live (Nov 8 evening):** every login has `created` equal to `last refresh`. The connector held an access token valid for a week, never needed the token endpoint, and still came back with a new client id on Nov 9, 10, 11 (three times), 12 and 14.
- **Before November:** logins lasted days to weeks (Oct 12 → Oct 29, Sep 29 → Oct 10). From Nov 3 they shrink to two days, then one, then less.
- **Claude Code control** (`JizYCK`): one login since Oct 12, still healthy.

(The script's date filter was off by a year, which is why you see rows back to September; it didn't affect the reading.)

## What that does to the workaround list

| Workaround | Verdict |
|---|---|
| Rotation replay for concurrent refreshes (#1194) | Ruled out: no refresh happens at all. |
| Root-path aliases for the fallback (#1169) | Not the trigger here, since the fallback starts from a failed refresh. Still cheap insurance. |
| Longer access tokens | Already done; the chain shows it didn't help. |
| CIMD | The only lever left. The connector throws away its client registration and tokens together; with CIMD there is no registration to lose. |

The Nov 3 onset lines up with other reports in the tracker dated Nov 2–4 (#1224, #1214, one commenter says "since about 2026-11-02"). That points to a change on Anthropic's side rather than anything we shipped; our last deploy before that was Oct 12.

## Recommendation

Build CIMD support plus the aliases and release it for a test. It is a bet, not a proven fix: if the connector also discards its tokens under a stable client id, the morning sign-in stays. The evidence for it is that Claude picks CIMD over dynamic registration when offered (#1194) and one operator reports CIMD sign-ins holding where the registered ones did not.

If CIMD doesn't stop it, the fallback is to use the local `ctxlayer` entry on your machine (the Claude Code path, which has held one login since Oct 12) rather than the hosted connector.

input.recap: CIMD support and the root-path OAuth aliases are built and the full verify suite passes. Nothing is committed or deployed, and the change also touches the routing template in the ctxlayer-ops repo. Whether it stops the morning sign-in can only be seen after a release.

content.text:
CIMD support and the root-path aliases are built, and `bun run verify` passes (731 unit, 55 web, 537 integration). Nothing is committed or deployed.

## What changed

- **CIMD on:** the provider now accepts a client's published metadata URL as its `client_id` and advertises that in the discovery document. Dynamic registration stays available. It had never been enabled before, despite the compat flag being set.
- **Sign-in keeps earlier logins for CIMD clients:** a CIMD client id is shared by Desktop, web and mobile, so the library default of revoking the user's previous grant would sign the other surfaces out. That revoke is now skipped for CIMD clients only; the nightly idle sweep still retires unused ones.
- **Root-path aliases:** `/token`, `/register` and `/authorize` now behave exactly like `/oauth/token`, `/oauth/register` and `/oauth/authorize`.
- **Asset routing:** those three paths are added to `run_worker_first` in `wrangler.toml` and in `../ctxlayer-ops/wrangler.template.toml`. The second is in the ops repo, which I edited because yukitools renders its config from it; without it the aliases would not take effect there.
- **Admin clients viewer:** CIMD logins have no stored client record, so the viewer now adds a row for each CIMD client that holds a login. This part has no test.

The new tests cover the aliases (register, code exchange, refresh via the root paths) and a full CIMD sign-in and refresh with nothing written to the client store.

## What is not known yet

- **Whether your existing connector switches to CIMD on its own.** One report shows an explicit "Use Claude's published identity (CIMD)" option in the add-connector dialog, so you may have to remove and re-add the connector after the release.
- **Whether a stable client id stops the connector discarding its tokens.** That only shows after a release.

## After you release

1. `https://mcp.yukitools.dev/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` should show `client_id_metadata_document_supported: true`.
2. `POST https://mcp.yukitools.dev/token` should no longer return 405.
3. Sign in once more, then rerun the login-chain script. The script prints only the first six characters of the client id, so a CIMD login shows as `https:`. If the morning prompts then stop, the bet paid off.

The main files are [provider-config.ts](apps/worker/src/oauth/provider-config.ts), [default-endpoints.ts](apps/worker/src/oauth/default-endpoints.ts), [cimd.ts](apps/worker/src/oauth/cimd.ts) and [complete-mcp.ts](apps/worker/src/idp/complete-mcp.ts).
Commit both

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Roll the app repo's CURRENT checkout out to ctxlayer deployments
# (scenario B). Re-renders each per-host config from the template + registry
# (so it works on a fresh app checkout), then migrate THEN deploy.
#
# This is the ONLY upgrade path — nothing auto-upgrades. Each host keeps
# running whatever commit it was last released with (visible in the SPA
# footer / GET /api/health), so upgrades are deliberate and stageable.
#
# Usage:
#   [APP_REPO=/path/to/ctxlayer] scripts/release-all.sh                 # all hosts in tenants.json
#   scripts/release-all.sh dev stage          # only these hosts
#   scripts/release-all.sh --migrate-only     # apply migrations, skip deploy
set -euo pipefail

OPS_ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
APP_REPO="${APP_REPO:-$(cd "$OPS_ROOT/../ctxlayer" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)}"
[[ -n "$APP_REPO" && -f "$APP_REPO/wrangler.toml" ]] || {
  echo "✗ APP_REPO not found (sibling ../ctxlayer). Set APP_REPO=/path/to/ctxlayer." >&2
  exit 1
}
TEMPLATE="$OPS_ROOT/wrangler.template.toml"
REGISTRY="$OPS_ROOT/tenants.json"
[ -s "$REGISTRY" ] || { echo "✗ no tenant registry at $REGISTRY." >&2; exit 1; }

# Preflight: fail fast on deploy-scheme naming drift (binding/cron parity) so a
# templated tenant can't silently lose a binding or a queue/cron consumer.
APP_REPO="$APP_REPO" "$OPS_ROOT/scripts/check-deploy-scheme.sh"

MIGRATE_ONLY=0
SELECTED=()
for a in "$@"; do
  if [[ "$a" == "--migrate-only" ]]; then MIGRATE_ONLY=1; else SELECTED+=("$a"); fi
done
if [[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -eq 0 ]]; then
  # No `mapfile`/`readarray` — macOS ships bash 3.2, where they don't exist.
  while IFS= read -r slug; do SELECTED+=("$slug"); done < <(jq -r 'keys[]' "$REGISTRY")
fi
[[ ${#SELECTED[@]} -gt 0 ]] || { echo "✗ nothing to release." >&2; exit 1; }

# Cross-account guard (see docs/yukitools-provisioning.md): keep only the
# selected hosts that live in the ACTIVE Cloudflare account. The active account
# is CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID when a per-account token is exported, else the satisa
# OAuth login wrangler defaults to. A tenant's account is its registry `account`
# (entries without one predate multi-account and live in satisa). The accounts
# use different tokens that AREN'T in the registry, so deploying a tenant against
# the wrong login would create resources in the wrong account (or fail) —
# mismatched hosts are skipped here, BEFORE the build, so a wrong-creds run fails
# fast. Run release-all.sh once per account with that account's creds exported.
SATISA_ACCOUNT="${SATISA_ACCOUNT:-a65126d6fa58bfd6da28c3504b0aa859}"
ACTIVE_ACCOUNT="${CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID:-$SATISA_ACCOUNT}"
DEPLOYABLE=()
for SLUG in "${SELECTED[@]}"; do
  TENANT_ACCOUNT=$(jq -r --arg s "$SLUG" '.[$s].account // ""' "$REGISTRY")
  TENANT_ACCOUNT="${TENANT_ACCOUNT:-$SATISA_ACCOUNT}"
  if [[ "$TENANT_ACCOUNT" != "$ACTIVE_ACCOUNT" ]]; then
    echo "⏭ $SLUG: in account $TENANT_ACCOUNT ≠ active $ACTIVE_ACCOUNT — skipping (export that account's creds to deploy it)." >&2
    continue
  fi
  DEPLOYABLE+=("$SLUG")

## One fix on the way out

The first release (`d299f37`) had a flaw I caught in the live checks. On the MCP host, `/oauth/authorize` sits behind Cloudflare Access, and my `/authorize` alias served the page in place, skipping that gate. The result was a consent page with only a Deny button. It was not a bypass: the worker re-verifies the Access identity itself, so nothing could be approved without it.

I changed `/authorize` to a redirect to `/oauth/authorize`, reran verify (all green), committed it as `4f8131c`, pushed and re-released. The flawed version was live for about three minutes.

- **Existing logins:** this session's Claude Code connection still works after the release.

2. If it does, remove the connector and add it again; if the dialog offers "Use Claude's published identity (CIMD)", pick it.

That doesn't explain why this stopped working and we do not have another AI
service to test at this time. We also opened a ticket with Anthropic, this
was their reply.
We traced the reference you sent, along with the failed connections across
your organization. Claude's connections to your n8n server started failing
at about 7 PM Pacific on November 3 (03:00 UTC on November 4). Since then,
every request Claude has sent to your n8n server's OAuth token endpoint,
which is the step that completes a sign-in and keeps each person's
connection refreshed, has come back with HTTP 500, an internal server error
from n8n. Just before that, at about 6:55 PM Pacific, Claude's regular
requests to n8n also began failing with the connection dropping
mid-request. Other parts of n8n's sign-in are still responding normally,
including the sign-in page and n8n accepting Claude as a client.
​
That's why everyone's connection lapsed, and why pressing Reconnect fails:
each person signs in to n8n successfully, and n8n then returns an error
when Claude collects the token. Removing and adding the connector again in
Claude won't get past this, since the attempt in your screenshot was
already a brand-new registration that n8n had accepted before the token
step failed. There's also no need for members to keep retrying in the
meantime.
​
The next step is on the n8n server itself. Two things should help your n8n
admin find the cause:
​
   - The list of permissions (scopes) your n8n server publishes to Claude
   changed between yesterday evening and this morning, from 16 down to 9,
   which suggests the server was updated or reconfigured around the time this
   started. Anything that changed or failed on the server between about 6:50
   and 7:15 PM Pacific on November 3, such as an update, a rollback, a
   restart, or a configuration change, is the first place to look.
   - The n8n server logs should show the actual error. For example, the
   attempt in your screenshot reached n8n's token endpoint at 12:01:21 PM
   Pacific today (20:01:21 UTC).
​
Once n8n answers those token requests normally again, we'd expect most
members' connections to start working on their own the next time they use
the connector. Anyone who's still asked to reconnect can press Reconnect
once, and it should sign them in.
​
I hope this helps, but let me know if I haven't quite got this right. If
the n8n logs don't point to a clear cause, please send me the errors you
find there, and I'll be happy to assist however I can.
Ryan Colley

content.text:
No, neither the issue nor the changelog has a fix for the daily reconnect. The issue has one useful hint, but it's a guess.

## The n8n issue (n8n-io/n8n#43048)

**It's a different failure from ours.** From about Nov 4, nobody at that company could sign in at all. Anthropic support traced it: n8n's token endpoint answered every request with an HTTP 500 error. Our token endpoint returns 200 every time; the connector just throws the login away.

**Nobody posted a fix.** The customer reported "working for now" on Nov 12 without saying what changed. n8n's bot closed the issue twice with a generic "fix in an upcoming release" message. The maintainer reopened it, saying their investigation points to "a regression on Anthropic side".

**The useful part is the maintainer's hypothesis.** Claude's apps switched by default to the newest MCP protocol version (2026-07-28) around early November. Servers that don't support it hit a fallback path in Claude, which the maintainer suspects is buggy. They connected fine from the newest Claude app to an n8n version that supports 2026-07-28.

That fits our case in two ways:
- **Our server doesn't support 2026-07-28 either.** Claude probes for it, gets a 400, and falls back to the older handshake; we saw this in the logs on Nov 9.
- **The timing matches.** Our logins started shrinking from Nov 3.

But it is unproven. The maintainer's version is about the token endpoint, which isn't what fails for us, and "connected once" says nothing about whether a login survives the next morning.

## The n8n changelog

I checked n8n's merged changes since October (n8n is on 2.48 now). The OAuth and MCP work is almost all about n8n as a client of other MCP servers, plus telemetry. I found nothing that changes how n8n's own MCP server handles Claude's sign-in or refresh, and no entry mentions reconnect prompts.

## What it means for us

Testing the hypothesis means supporting MCP 2026-07-28 natively. That is the McpAgent migration we parked on Nov 9: a stateless redesign, not a flag. I wouldn't start it on this evidence alone. A stronger trigger would be an Anthropic reply on #1237, or a report from an operator whose server supports 2026-07-28 that the daily prompt went away.
plan the MCP 2026-07-28 migration

---

## 1. `McpSessionDO`: `apps/worker/src/mcp/session-do.ts` (840 lines)

**Class:** `export class McpSessionDO extends McpAgent<Env, undefined, McpProps>` (L81). The state type is `undefined`, so `this.state` / `this.setState` are never used.

**Instance fields**
- `server = new McpServer({name:'ctxlayer',version:'0.1.0'},{instructions: SERVER_INSTRUCTIONS})` (L82-85). It is built eagerly, then reassigned inside `init()` in two places (L99, L161).
- `private upstreamProxy: UpstreamProxyRegistry | null = null` (L87).

**Methods**
- `async init()` (L89-773). This is the only override. The repo has no `onStart`, `fetch`, `alarm` or `onConnect` override. The `agents` 0.33 `McpAgent.onStart(props)` calls `init()` on every DO start or wake, and then `reinitializeServer()` replays the stored `initializeRequest`.
- `private docMarkdown(docId)` (L792-797): reads from R2 only (snapshot, then `source.md`).
- `private stageUsage(args)` (L799-808): calls `stageUsageRow(this.ctx.storage.sql, …)` and then `this.schedule(5, 'flushUsageOutbox', undefined, {idempotent:true})`.
- `async flushUsageOutbox()` (L818-834): an alarm callback that the SDK dispatches by name. It calls `drainOutbox(sql, env.USAGE_QUEUE)`, reschedules after 5s while rows remain, and retries after 30s on failure.

**Use of DO primitives**
- `this.ctx.storage.sql`:
  - L111 `ensureOutboxTable`
  - L337 and L735 `sqliteHintLedger(...)`
  - L801 `stageUsageRow`
  - L819 drain
- `this.schedule(...)`: L802, L824, L830. All three schedule `flushUsageOutbox`.
- `this.props`: L90, L188, L235 (whoami dumps the whole props object), L244, 287, 306, 324, 412, 448 (`role !== 'admin'`), 482, 553, 571, 576, 602, 634, 656, 661 (`role`).
- `this.getSessionId()`: L189, L335, L731. It parses the DO name `streamable-http:<sessionId>`.
- `this.sql` and `this.setState`: not used.

**What `agents` 0.33 `McpAgent` itself keeps in DO storage**

Source: `node_modules/.bun/agents@0.33.0+50eaea991f04e17b/node_modules/agents/dist/mcp/index.js`.
- `"props"` (L1619, L1629)
- `"initializeRequest"` (L1480-1483)
- per-stream request ids `STREAM_REQS_KEY_PREFIX` (L1501-1505)
- `DurableObjectEventStore(this.ctx.storage)` for SSE resumability (`getEventStore`)
- the schedule table that backs `this.schedule`

**Wiring**
- `apps/worker/src/oauth/provider-config.ts:89`:
  ```ts
  apiHandlers = { '/mcp': McpSessionDO.serve('/mcp', { binding: 'MCP_SESSION_DO' }) }
  ```
  `/mcp` is the only API handler. `/sse` was dropped (comment at L76-79). The OAuth resource is `mcpResourceUrl(env)` (L94).
- `apps/worker/src/index.ts`:
  - L27 `export { McpSessionDO } from './mcp/session-do'`
  - L45-48 `buildOAuthProvider(env)` runs per request
  - L59 `isMcpPathOnWrongHost` check
  - L66 `buildOAuthProvider(env).fetch(...)`
- `apps/worker/src/env.ts:76` declares `MCP_SESSION_DO: DurableObjectNamespace`.
- `serve()` in agents (index.js L107-182, L284-299, L356-368): it reads the `mcp-session-id` header and calls `getAgentByName(namespace, 'streamable-http:'+sessionId, { props: ctx.props })`. GET with `mcp-session-id` is the standalone SSE stream (L530). DELETE goes to the agent without props (L368).

## 2. Tool registration and init cost

**Built-ins.** Title and description come from `builtinToolMeta()` in `packages/shared/src/builtin-tools.ts`. Input shapes come from `apps/worker/src/mcp/builtin-schemas.ts`.

| Tool | Location |
|---|---|
| whoami | session-do.ts L230 |
| list_my_context | L239 |
| list_upstreams | L276 |
| describe_upstream | L297 |
| reload_upstreams | L322 |
| get_doc | L382 |
| search_docs | L402 |
| active_users | L436 |
| poll_task | L469 |
| list_tasks | L551 |
| draft_skill | L629 |
| save_draft_skill | L651 |
| list_skills, get_skill | `skill-mcp.ts` L45 and L95, via `registerSkillMcp(...)` at session-do L571 |

Every built-in is wrapped in the `rec(...)` usage recorder (L180-224). That wrapper captures `this.getSessionId()` and calls `this.stageUsage`. Built-in handlers do all their D1 work per call, and none of them reads DO state except through `rec`. The exception is `reload_upstreams`, which mutates `this.upstreamProxy` and the live `this.server`.

**Proxied upstream tools.** These live in `UpstreamProxyRegistry`, `apps/worker/src/mcp/proxy-registry.ts`.
- Constructor (L152-168): `(env, userId, stageUsage, sessionId, makeClient, hintLedger, catalogueBudgetMs)`.
- Built at session-do L727-737, using `sqliteHintLedger(this.ctx.storage.sql)` and `init(this.server, upstreamCtx)`.
- In-memory per-session state (L118-150):
  - `clients` (upstream_id → `UpstreamClient`)
  - `rows`
  - `boundStamp` (the credential `updated_at` at bind time)
  - `unbound`
  - `binding` (in-flight binds)
  - `allowedToolKeys` (ACL-allowed set, also checked at call time)
  - `firstResultHints`
- `registerTool` (L587-773): one `server.registerTool(mangled, {title, description, inputSchema}, handler)` per allowed cached tool. The input schema comes from `jsonSchemaToZod(JSON.parse(row.input_schema))`.

**Init path, once per DO start or wake.** The comments at proxy-registry L91-96 and bearer.ts L140 say that hibernation wakes re-run it.
1. `findById(env, userId)`: user status gate (session-do L97). 1 D1.
2. `loadUserContext` (`catalogue-views.ts` L83-91): `listUpstreamsVisibleToUser`, then parallel `listSkillsForUpstreams` and `listDocsForUpstreams`. 3 D1 round trips.
3. `getUserCredentialStatuses(...)` for the connection alert (session-do L146). 1 D1.
4. `registerSkillPrompts` → `listPublishedSkills` (`skill-mcp.ts` L182). 1 D1.
5. `registry.init` → `registerUpstreams` (proxy-registry L309-391):
   - Parallel: `resolveUserPrincipals` (calls `resolveUserScope` and `listUserRoleIds`, `tool-access.ts` L33), `listToolAccessForUpstreams` (1 D1), and `listCachedToolsForUpstreams` (1 D1, batched across all upstreams).
   - Then **per upstream, concurrently**, `prepareUpstream` (L461-488):
     - `resolveUserUpstreamBearer` (`upstream/bearer.ts` L59-207):
       - `shared_bearer` / `user_bearer`: 1 D1 read plus AES decrypt.
       - `user_oauth`: `provider.tokens()` (1 D1 read via `getUserCredential`, `oauth-provider.ts` L225-227). If the token is fresh it is used directly. If it is within 5 min of expiry: a `getUserCredentialStatus` read, a D1 lease (`oauth-refresh.ts`), and an **outbound token-endpoint POST**. A permanent failure writes the reauth flag, audit and grant-observation rows.
     - If there is no bearer but a credential exists: `getUserCredentialStatus` (1 D1), and the upstream is listed unbound.
     - `makeClient(conn, bearer)` does no network I/O. `UpstreamHttpClient.ensureConnected` connects lazily (`http-client.ts` L99-160).
     - `ensureCatalogue` (L540-565): **uses the D1 cache** (`upstream_tools`, 24h TTL, L86). Only when the cache is empty or stale does it call **live `tools/list`** (MCP connect plus list, 60s per-call timeout). That call is raced against `CATALOGUE_REFRESH_BUDGET_MS = 10_000` and is followed by `replaceCachedTools` and `listCachedTools`.
   - Then `getUserCredentialStatuses` for the bound stamps. 1 D1.
6. DO-SQLite DDL: `ensureOutboxTable` and `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hinted_upstreams`.
7. CPU cost: `jsonSchemaToZod` for every registered tool.

KV reads on the init path: none in ctxlayer code. `OAUTH_KV` is read by the OAuth provider in the Worker before the DO is reached, and by `oauth-provider.ts` only for PKCE.

Not determined: the exact number of queries inside `listUpstreamsVisibleToUser` and `resolveUserScope`.

**Per proxied tool call** (handler, L636-751):
1. ACL backstop against `allowedToolKeys`.
2. **A6** `checkCredentialFreshness`: 1 D1 point read for user-scoped strategies.
3. Async path: `submitAsyncJob`.
4. Otherwise `ensureBound(conn, fresh.status)`. This rebinds if the stamp changed (`bind` resolves the bearer again and re-reads the status).
5. `runUpstreamCall` + `callWithHeartbeat` → `client.callTool`. The first call on a new client does the upstream MCP `initialize` handshake.
6. `deliverFirstResultHint` (hint ledger, DO SQLite).
7. `finally` → `this.stageUsage(...)` (DO SQLite plus schedule).

## 3. Per-session state

- **Usage outbox**
  - `apps/worker/src/usage/outbox.ts`: table `usage_outbox(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, msg TEXT)`. `USAGE_DRAIN_BATCH = 100`, and delivery is at-least-once (the consumer dedupes on event id).
  - Staged from session-do L799-808. Drained by `flushUsageOutbox` (L818-834) on a DO alarm with a 5s / 30s delay (L78-79).
  - The rationale is in the comments at L107-110 and in `usage/record.ts` L13: `waitUntil(queue.send)` was being cancelled after streaming responses ended.
  - `queues/jobs-consumer.ts` L153-175 already bypasses the outbox and calls `env.USAGE_QUEUE.send` directly.
- **Hint ledger**
  - `apps/worker/src/mcp/hint-ledger.ts`: table `hinted_upstreams(upstream_id PRIMARY KEY)`. It also has `inMemoryHintLedger()`, which tests use.
  - It is armed in `armFirstResultHint` (proxy-registry L400-410). Delivered in `deliverFirstResultHint` (L430-442, which also drops `structuredContent`), from the sync path (L733) and the async ack (L691).
  - The semantics are "once per upstream per session", and the key is implicitly the DO, i.e. the session id.
- **In-memory registry maps** (listed in section 2): rebuilt on every wake.

Verified in the installed code [I]:

- **`registerTool`:** the config is `{ title, description, inputSchema, outputSchema, annotations, icons, _meta }` (`d.mts:3300-3318`).
  - The preferred form takes a Standard Schema such as `z.object({...})`.
  - The raw-shape `{ field: z.string() }` form is `@deprecated` but still accepted.
  - Callbacks are `(args, ctx: ServerContext)` and return `CallToolResult | InputRequiredResult`.
- **`registerPrompt`:** takes `argsSchema` instead.
- **`registerResource`:** takes `(name, uri | ResourceTemplate, metadata & { cacheHint? }, cb)`.
- **Instructions:** `new McpServer(info, { instructions, capabilities, cacheHints, inputRequired, requestState })` (`d.mts:2762-2873`).
- **The `extra` → `ctx` change** (`d.mts:2073-2228`):

  | v1 | v2 |
  |---|---|
  | `extra.requestId` | `ctx.mcpReq.id` |
  | `extra.signal` | `ctx.mcpReq.signal` |
  | `extra._meta` | `ctx.mcpReq._meta` |
  | `extra.sendRequest` / `sendNotification` | `ctx.mcpReq.send` / `notify` |
  | (new) per-request envelope with client info and capabilities | `ctx.mcpReq.envelope` |
  | (new) MRTR state | `ctx.mcpReq.inputResponses`, `ctx.mcpReq.requestState<T>()` |
  | `extra.authInfo` | `ctx.http?.authInfo` |
  | request headers | `ctx.http?.req`, a web `Request` |
  | `extra.sessionId` | `ctx.sessionId` |

  - `ctx.mcpReq.elicitInput` and `requestSampling` throw on modern-era requests.
- **zod:** v2 depends on `zod ^4.2.0`. Your worker declares `^4.0.0`.
- **Tool-name validation:** `/^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$/`. It only warns (`console.warn`), it does not reject (`src-CX2iR2pK.mjs:7122-7180`).
- **Tasks:** the 2025-11-25 task types are "@deprecated 2025-11-25 wire vocabulary with no SDK runtime" in 2.0.0.
- **Caching:** `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` are emitted on modern list, read and discover results via `cacheHints`; 2025-era responses never carry them (`d.mts:2637-2656, 2788-2805`).

From the SDK v2 guides [W] (`https://ts.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/v2/migration/upgrade-to-v2.html` and `support-2026-07-28.html`):
- There is a codemod: `npx @modelcontextprotocol/codemod@latest v1-to-v2 .`
- `McpError` is renamed `ProtocolError`, and `ErrorCode` is renamed `ProtocolErrorCode`.
- "Zod v3 is no longer supported." Zod ≥4.2.0 self-converts.
- `registerResource` requires a metadata argument; pass `{}` if you have none.
- Resource-not-found is now -32602.
- Tasks: the experimental tasks feature was removed (SEP-2663). The later Tasks extension keeps `tasks/get` and `tasks/cancel`; this may only be in versions after 2.0.0.
- MRTR: the client retries up to `maxRounds` (default 10). The legacy shim uses 8 rounds and a 600 s timeout.
- `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` are required on modern POSTs. Missing or mismatched values get 400 with -32020.

Changelog (https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/changelog):
- Removes `Mcp-Session-Id` and sessions (SEP-2567).
- Removes `initialize` and `notifications/initialized`. "Every request now carries its protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta`" (SEP-2575).

- Roots, Sampling and Logging are deprecated.

# MCP 2026-07-28 migration: stateless MCP server, retire `McpSessionDO`

## Context

ctxlayer serves MCP through `McpAgent` (a Durable Object per MCP session, `apps/worker/src/mcp/session-do.ts`) on MCP SDK v1, which tops out at protocol `2025-11-25`. Claude's hosted clients now probe `server/discover` with `2026-07-28`, get our 400, and fall back to `initialize`.

Two reasons to move now:

- **The daily Reconnect prompt.** Token lifetime, CIMD and every refresh-path fix are ruled out (2026-11-15). The one untested lead is that Claude's fallback path for servers without `2026-07-28` is buggy (n8n maintainer's hypothesis; onset ~Nov 3 matches ours). Only answering `2026-07-28` natively tests it.
- **`McpAgent` is deprecated and feature-frozen** (agents ≥ 0.20). The supported path is `createMcpHandler` from `agents/mcp/server` + `@modelcontextprotocol/server` v2: a fresh server per request, no DO, no session.

Side benefits of stateless: no serial-DO bottleneck (a 2–3 min upstream call no longer blocks the session), no stale-session bearer (`reload_upstreams` gotcha), no hibernation re-init, user suspension checked on every request, and `/mcp` becomes testable in vitest.

**Outcome:** `/mcp` answers both `2026-07-28` and 2025-era clients from one stateless code path; `McpSessionDO` is deleted.

## Approach: two lanes first, then one

Run the new stateless server **beside** the DO, routed per request with the SDK's `isLegacyRequest()`:

- modern request (`2026-07-28` envelope) → new stateless handler, `legacy: 'reject'`
- legacy request (`initialize`, session id, GET/DELETE) → existing `McpSessionDO.serve()` untouched

Claude's hosted connector goes modern on day one (it probes modern first), so the Reconnect hypothesis is tested while Claude Code and other 2025-era clients keep the proven path. After a soak, flip the legacy lane to the stateless handler too and delete the DO. This is the pattern in Cloudflare's migrate-to-SDK-v2 guide.

The DO code is **frozen, not refactored**, during the overlap. New code goes in new modules and reuses the helpers that are already DO-independent.

## Design: what each piece of session state becomes

| Today (per-session DO) | Stateless replacement |
|---|---|
| `init()` builds everything once per session/wake (≈10 D1 reads + one bearer resolve per upstream + `jsonSchemaToZod` × ~460 tools) | **Build only what the request needs**, from `Mcp-Method` / `Mcp-Name` headers (modern) or a peek at the JSON-RPC body (legacy lane, phase 3). See "Request scope" below. |
| Usage outbox in DO SQLite + alarm drain (`usage/outbox.ts`, `flushUsageOutbox`) | `env.USAGE_QUEUE.send(buildUsageMsg(...))` awaited in the tool handler's `finally`, as `queues/jobs-consumer.ts` already does. The outbox existed only because `waitUntil` died after the DO's streamed response. |
| `session_id` (DO name) on `usage_events` / `async_jobs` | `sessionKey = short sha256(userId + ':' + oauth clientId)`: stable per user+client, no reader depends on the old meaning. No schema change. |
| Hint ledger in DO SQLite (`hint-ledger.ts`, once per upstream per session) | D1 table `mcp_hint_ledger(user_id, client_key, upstream_id, hinted_at)`, re-arm after 12 h. New `HintLedger` implementation behind the existing interface. **Migration 0039.** |
| Registry maps: `clients`, `boundStamp`, `unbound`, `allowedToolKeys` (`proxy-registry.ts`) | Gone. A `tools/call` resolves ACL, credential and bearer fresh, for the one upstream it names. A6 freshness (`credential-freshness.ts`) becomes inherent. |
| User-status gate at session start | `findById` on every request (suspension is instant even without grant revocation). |
| `instructions` composed at init | Composed when the request is `server/discover` (or legacy `initialize`), via existing `composeInstructions` / `connectionAlert` / `upstreamGuidance`. `cacheHints`: short private TTL so the "auto-refresh stopped" alert stays current. |
| `reload_upstreams` + `sendToolListChanged` | Lists are always current. Keep the tool (skills and docs reference it): it returns the current upstream list and calls `handler.notify.toolsChanged()` best-effort. |
| Progress heartbeat (`callWithHeartbeat`, `extra.sendNotification`) | `ctx.mcpReq.notify` on the per-request response stream. |
| Upstream client reused across a session | New `UpstreamHttpClient` per call (one extra upstream `initialize` round trip). Accept and measure; `jobs-consumer` already works this way. |

**Request scope** (the core of the new builder):

| Request | Registers | D1 / network |
|---|---|---|
| `server/discover`, `initialize` | nothing; instructions + capabilities only | user, context, credential statuses |
| `tools/list` | all built-ins + all ACL-allowed cached upstream tools (schemas from the `upstream_tools` cache; live refresh only when stale, existing 10 s budget) | no bearer resolves, no upstream connects |
| `tools/call` | the one named tool | built-in: its own queries. Upstream: ACL + one bearer + the call |
| `prompts/*`, `resources/*` | only that family | as today |

## Files

New, under `apps/worker/src/mcp/stateless/`:

- `handler.ts`: `/mcp` fetch handler. `isLegacyRequest` routing, `createMcpHandler(factory, { route: '/mcp', legacy: 'reject', allowedHostnames, allowedOriginHostnames })`, 415 for non-JSON bodies. Built per request with `env`/`ctx` in closure (same pattern as `buildOAuthProvider` in `index.ts`).
- `request-scope.ts`: derive `{ method, name }` from headers / body. Pure, unit-tested.
- `build-server.ts`: the factory. User gate → scope → register. Reads identity from `getMcpAuthContext().props` (`McpProps`) and `authInfo.clientId`.
- `builtin-tools.ts`: the 14 built-ins moved over from `session-do.ts` (handlers are already D1-only), on the v2 `registerTool` API.
- `upstream-tools.ts`: list + call for proxied tools. Reuses `runUpstreamCall` / `callWithHeartbeat` (`mcp/upstream-call-runner.ts`), `resolveUserUpstreamBearer` (`upstream/bearer.ts`), `isToolAllowed` + `listUpstreamsVisibleToUser`, `submitAsyncJob` (`mcp/async-submit.ts`), `scrubErrorContent` / sanitisers (`mcp/result-postprocess.ts`, `mcp/provenance.ts`), `deliverFirstResultHint` logic.
- `usage.ts`: direct queue send + `sessionKey`.
- `hint-ledger-d1.ts` + `db/queries/hint-ledger.ts` + `db/migrations/0039_mcp_hint_ledger.sql`.

Changed:

- `oauth/provider-config.ts`: `apiHandlers['/mcp']` → `{ fetch }` from `stateless/handler.ts` (which delegates legacy requests to `McpSessionDO.serve` during the overlap).
- `mcp/skill-mcp.ts`, `mcp/skill-sep2640.ts`: accept the v2 `McpServer` (prompt/resource registration; `registerResource` needs a metadata arg).
- `apps/worker/package.json`: add `@modelcontextprotocol/server@2.4.0` (exact, agents peer), align `@modelcontextprotocol/client@2.4.0`, `zod ^4.2.0`.

Deleted in phase 4: `mcp/session-do.ts`, `mcp/proxy-registry.ts`, `mcp/hint-ledger.ts` (SQLite half), `mcp/credential-freshness.ts`, `usage/outbox.ts`, `mcp/json-schema-to-zod.ts` if v2 takes JSON Schema directly, their tests.

Out of scope: the outbound upstream client stays on SDK v1 (`upstream/http-client.ts` and the upstream OAuth files); migrating it to `@modelcontextprotocol/client` v2 is separate.

## Phases

**0. Spike (throwaway worktree + dev tenant, nothing merged).** Resolve the unknowns before committing to the design:
- `bun add` the v2 server at 2.4.0; confirm typecheck and that 2.4.0's API matches what was read in the stray 2.0.0 copy.
- Minimal stateless `/mcp` behind the OAuth provider: props and `clientId` reach a tool; `server/discover` answers; a progress notification streams; awaited `USAGE_QUEUE.send` lands a row.
- Can v2 `registerTool` take upstream JSON Schema without zod conversion? If not, keep `jsonSchemaToZod`.
- Does `agents/mcp/server` load in vitest workerd (no `cloudflare:email`)? Decides whether `/mcp` gets end-to-end tests.
- Connect Claude Desktop's hosted connector to the dev tenant and confirm in Workers Logs that it stays on the modern lane.
- Cost check: time `tools/list` and one upstream `tools/call` on the stateless path.

**1. Build the modern lane** (modules above), DO untouched. Tests: unit for `request-scope`; integration through the real handler for discover, list (ACL + visibility: ungranted upstream indistinguishable from nonexistent), call (success, thrown upstream error → generic code + `ref=`, `isError` passthrough scrubbed), hint once, usage row, suspended user refused. `bun run verify`.

**2. Ship two-lane + soak.** Canary dev → stage → OG → yukitools (migration 0039 first). Watch for a week: share of requests per lane, error rate per lane, usage rows, and the login chain (`oauth_grant_activity`) for the Reconnect verdict.

**Decision gate.** If Reconnects stop: hypothesis confirmed, report on #1237, continue. If they persist: the migration still stands on the deprecation, but phase 3 loses urgency; decide whether to continue now or park with both lanes running.

**3. Legacy lane → stateless.** Switch the handler to `legacy: 'stateless'` and stop routing to the DO. Known behaviour changes for 2025-era clients: no `Mcp-Session-Id`, GET SSE → 405, no `tools/list_changed`. Verify Claude Code, Claude Desktop local config and one non-Claude client against stage first.

**4. Delete the DO.** One release with the DO unreferenced (lets outboxes drain), then remove the class, binding and export, add a `[[migrations]] tag = "v2" deleted_classes = ["McpSessionDO"]` in `wrangler.toml` **and** `../ctxlayer-ops/wrangler.template.toml`, delete the files listed above, and update `CLAUDE.md` + `docs/PLAN.md` where they describe `McpSessionDO`.

## Risks

- **Per-request cost.** A cold `tools/list` reads the whole cached catalogue each time. Mitigated by request scoping and `cacheHints` TTL on list results; measured in the spike.
- **Hosted clients on the modern lane are new territory** (their `2026-07-28` support is weeks old). The two-lane design limits blast radius; rollback is flipping the handler back to DO-only.
- **agents' legacy lane rejects server→client requests.** We use none (no elicitation or sampling), only progress notifications; confirm those work in phase 3.
- **SDK 2.4.0 was not inspected** (only 2.0.0 is on disk). Phase 0 exists to close that.
- **DO deletion is irreversible** and drops any undrained usage rows; hence the drain release before it.

## Verification

- `bun run verify` at every phase.
- Dev tenant, per lane: `curl` `server/discover` with `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28` (200 + instructions) and a legacy `initialize` (still served).
- Real clients: Claude Desktop hosted connector (modern), Claude Code (legacy until phase 3): `whoami`, `list_upstreams`, one proxied call per auth strategy, one async tool + `poll_task`, a skill prompt, a doc resource.
- D1 after calls: `usage_events` rows with the new `session_id`, `mcp_hint_ledger` row after a first upstream result.
- Reconnect verdict: rerun the login-chain query daily during the soak; success = no new hosted sign-in for a week.
